newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court rejects appeal in Lloyds's case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court rejects appeal in Lloyds's case.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court Monday denied an appeal of a ruling ordering the dismissal of a lawsuit seeking to force Lloyd's of London to provide more information about a multibillion-dollar restructuring.

The justices, without comment or dissent, let stand a ruling by a U.S. appeals court in August that threw out a judge's injunction barring the restructing. The decision allowed the $2.2 billion reorganization to win approval.
The lawsuit had been brought by a group of U.S. investors, or Names as they are known at Lloyd's.

A federal judge in Virginia in August said Lloyd's sold securities to U.S. Names in violation of federal securities laws. He granted the injunction and ordered Lloyd's to provide more information to U.S. investors by Sept. 23.
But the Baltimore-based appeals court overturned the ruling, ordering the judge to dismiss the lawsuit.

In their Supreme Court appeal, lawyers for the investors said the appeals court agreed to quickly hear Lloyd's request for a stay of the preliminary injuction. They argued that the appeals court erred, exceeding its authority, by deciding the merits of the case.

Attorneys for Lloyd's replied that the appeals court had the power to expedite the case and to dismiss the lawsuit. They said the appeals court followed well-established precedent and committed no legal error.
